ownerDecisions.question: Dismiss these authenticated routes' js/missing-rate-limiting alerts as "won't fix", or put a rate-limit middleware CodeQL recognises (express-rate-limit or similar) in front of /api. A middleware closes them in one change but adds a dependency and a shared limit that can throttle the owner's own phone; none of these routes is reachable from the internet without a credential.

GET/PUT /api/files/text resolve and confine the path, then read/write it by pathname. A same-user process can swap a symlink in between (documented residual, docs/SECURITY.md:72). Note that this includes a sandboxed job of a non-browser agent with exec: its sandbox denies Reach's data dir but lets it write its shared folder. docs/SECURITY.md:71 already says shell-capable agents are not sandboxed by API scopes. Accept (won't fix) or move these routes to the descriptor helper browser agents use.
Full control's direct write branch (lstat then open by path) keeps the same-user swap residual; Full control is OS-user power by design. Accept (won't fix)?

A guest's pending admission receipt (request secret and the invitation secret) is kept in sessionStorage so a reload resumes the wait. Accept (won't fix, documented at docs/SECURITY.md:140), or drop it on reload at the cost of a re-join.

alerts.reason: Real, availability. POST /api/browser/tools/run (Full control and Apps agents) works out a salted scrypt fingerprint of the run's inputs (~30 ms, 16 MiB, on libuv's 4-thread pool) before any run budget: on every replay of a requestId already in the ledger, and for a new run before the browser check, so neither spends the 1000-run ledger or the single-run slot. A tailnet agent (no gateway limiter) flooding either path kept all four threads busy and stalled Reach's file, zlib and crypto work for everyone. Fingerprints are now worked out one at a time across all agents (requests wait their turn; none refused; results unchanged). The scanner looks for rate-limit middleware, so this alert will likely stay open after the fix.

alerts.reason: Oct 12 Windows code. `reach cli` checked existsSync(reach.cmd) then wrote it, so a reach.cmd another tool created in between was overwritten despite the 'Reach left it alone' promise. The folder is the user's own (~\.local\bin or WindowsApps), so no privilege boundary, but the promise now holds: the shim is created exclusively ('wx'); on EEXIST it is read, and overwritten only if it is another Reach folder's shim.

alerts.reason: Same code as #171 (prior: local-mutation residual), renumbered after an Oct 12 edit on a nearby line. SKILL.md was measured by path (stat) and read by path again, so a file that grew in between was read whole past the 256 KB cap. Now opened once (O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO is refused at once), measured and read through that handle, bounded to 256 KB. The install's check hash still covers exactly the text read.
